result.title: WanderBench: Can World Models Explore Dynamic Worlds from Video?
result.summary: Video world models conditioned on an input video make it possible to explore real, recorded dynamic scenes, enabling re-shooting of footage, free-viewpoint replay, and real-to-sim environments for embodied agents. Such uses require the generated rollout to stay faithful to the recorded world, yet existing benchmarks start from a single image or a text prompt, and video-conditioned generation is evaluated mainly on perceptual quality and camera following. These evaluations do not directly assess whether exploration preserves subject identity, event progression, and scene consistency upon revisiting a location. We introduce WanderBench, a benchmark for exploring dynamic worlds from video. It comprises 745 single-shot source videos of real and AI-generated content in three difficulty tiers (3-25 s), paired with camera routes given as keyboard actions, and evaluates six dimensions with 24 human-validated sub-metrics. Benchmarking eight models, we find that as clips grow longer, models keep the static scene and visual quality but lose camera control and the source dynamics, and that none keeps revisited places consistent. We further propose WanderLand, a training-free framework that conditions each frame of a frozen model on the same-instant source and, on revisits, on its own earlier static content. WanderLand improves five models on every dimension, by up to 8.3 points in source-dynamics fidelity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 WanderBench，用 745 段单镜头视频、键盘式相机路线和 24 项人工校验子指标，评测视频条件世界模型在长时探索中是否保持主体身份、事件进程与重访地点一致性；并给出免训练框架 WanderLand，让冻结模型每帧同时条件于同刻源帧与自身先前静态内容。
AI.relevance_reason: 其发现「时长生后保留静态场景与画质却丢失源动态、重访不一致」与 LVR 关心的长程信息坍缩相近；逐帧重注入同刻视觉证据、重访时复用自身早前内容的做法，可能可供核查为视觉旁路或证据筛选机制。
